### W385 shell read-block guard (2026-11-11, verified product)

The host already carried `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` for directory grants but did not apply it to shell reads; a simple `cat /outside/secret` could be allowed when an outer `Bash(cat:*)` rule matched. `applyShellReadings` now calls `shellReadBlockDecision` when the flag is true. It parses the command with `E6`/`vS`, unwraps `sudo`/`env`/`command`/`timeout`-style launchers, restricts to simple/directory read commands (`ls`/`du`/`tree` included) and pattern-first readers (`grep`/`rg`/`sed`/`awk` skip their program/pattern argument), expands a leading `~`/`~/`, expands glob operands with the filesystem and checks every match, resolves operands and `<`/`<>` redirect targets against the workspace cwd plus their realpath identity, and returns a readings ask when any lexical or resolved path falls outside the workspace, `additionalDirectories` or session grant roots. The owned plan file and its `-agent-*` `.md` variants are exempt. Matching `read_file` input rules take precedence: deny rules deny, ask rules ask, and allow rules exempt the operand. `/dev/null`, stdio and tty are exempt; commands without the flag are unchanged.

This is a conservative subset of the source read-block chain (`vX` [3151331,3156825), `sR` and the `hTr` path checks in `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js` SHA-256 `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`). Sandbox state, skill/registry launch ancestry and the full source callback chain remain open under #123. Product tests cover outside ask, inside allow, no-flag allow, `/dev/null` exemption, read redirects, `~` expansion, glob matches, realpath/symlink identity, read allow/ask/deny rules, session grant roots, pattern-first readers, directory readers, launcher unwrapping and the owned/agent plan-file exemption. Permissions/shell suites, 18-case driver and check/build pass; no original-application execution was performed.

### W385 nested `bash -c` denial (2026-11-10, verified product)

The observed host miss allowed `bash -c 'rm -rf /tmp/x'` when `Bash(bash -c:*)` was allowed and `Bash(rm:*)` denied. `applyShellReadings` now calls `nestedShellDenial` before its early rule gate: it parses the outer command with `E6`/`vS`, unwraps a direct or wrapper-prefixed shell argv (`sudo`/`doas`/`env`/`command`/`builtin`/`nohup`/`time`/`timeout`/`nice`/`stdbuf`/`exec`), finds a `-c`-containing flag, and re-checks the script with `decideOnce`, recursing to depth 3. A nested deny returns deny; a nested rule ask is retained; other asks remain with the baseline.

This adapts the source nested policy (`jcn` [3213895,3215588), `Fcn` [3243430,3246934) in `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js` SHA-256 `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`). `nestedPrefixDenial` additionally runs the inner `pyr` declaration-prefix readings and denies any sampled command; a four-prefix inner script ending in a denied `rm` now denies, while a benign four-prefix script still allows. At depth greater than 3, a still-nested shell returns a readings ask instead of an allow. Sandbox state, the full declaration budget and the complete source callback chain remain open under #122. Product tests cover allow-outer/deny-inner, `-lc`, benign inner, `sudo`/`env` wrappers, nested `bash -c` depth, an explicit inner ask rule and inner four-prefix sampling. Permissions/shell suites, 18-case driver and check/build pass; no original-application execution was performed.

A granted external directory can create and update files through an ancestor directory symlink inside the grant. `outside/aliasdir/created.txt` with `aliasdir` → `real` previously failed `write_file: directory backup unavailable` because the missing-backup probe, retained backup copy and native publication used the lexical relative path. `Session.recordMissingDirectoryBackup` and `publishDirectoryFileTransaction` now accept an optional resolved grant-relative path, and `captureDirectoryBackup` copies from it for existing targets; the write tool passes `path.relative(grant.root, resolvedLanding)` when it differs from the lexical relative, while `lexicalPath` remains the policy/witness identity. ### W385 source-stash write lane integration (2026-11-10, verified product)

The Agent records the approved write observation in the copied `PathApprovalCall` write lane at tool lookup (`record('write', observation.requested, observation.spellings)`) and after each authorized input rewrite. ### W385 write approval-time path observation (2026-11-10, verified product)

A status callback that retargeted an ancestor directory link after a `write_file` ask was approved could redirect the write to a protected file: the read-only approval observation did not cover write tools, and the terminal-leaf check does not see an ancestor retarget. The Agent now captures `observePermissionPath` for `write_file`, `edit_file` and `notebook_edit` immediately after tool lookup (before PermissionRequest/PreToolUse hooks), recaptures after an authorized input rewrite, and before execution rejects a changed input path, changed landing/spellings or a live deny. The error is `<tool>: write approval changed`.

The live-deny recheck is skipped for the current write: a `PermissionRequest` allow that adopts plan mode authorizes the current call, and only later calls are denied. The landing/input check above remains the retarget guard; an ancestor retarget still fails. This preserves the source's current-call authorization without retroactively applying the newly adopted deny to the call that adopted it.

### W385 external ancestor-link create boundary (2026-11-10, diagnosed; design handoff)

The in-workspace ancestor-link create fix does not extend to a granted external directory. For `outside/aliasdir/created.txt` (`aliasdir` → `real` inside `outside`), the write reaches `Session.recordMissingDirectoryBackup`; that method derives `relative = path.relative(grant.root, lexicalPath)` and calls `probeMissingDirectoryFile({fd, relative})`, which walks the symlinked ancestor and refuses it, so the tool reports `write_file: directory backup unavailable` and never publishes. `publishDirectoryFileTransaction` also receives the lexical path.

A source-compatible adaptation needs a resolved grant-relative path carried through the missing-backup, publication, receipt and cold readers together with the lexical path, while refusing any link whose resolved parent leaves the grant. This is an #11 owner/backup boundary; the leaf check is not involved. The in-workspace path remains fixed and tested.

### W385 ancestor-link create fix (2026-11-10, verified product)

`confineResolved` previously rejected any unresolved leaf with a nonempty hop list as a dangling symlink. That also refused creating a file under an in-workspace ancestor directory symlink (e.g. `aliasdir/file.txt`, `aliasdir` → `real`) even though `real` is a real directory inside the workspace. The resolver now distinguishes the terminal `leafIsSymlink` bit from ancestor hops: a missing leaf is allowed only when `path.dirname(resolved.path)` is within an allowed root and is an existing directory. A terminal link to a missing target, a link whose parent lands outside/ungranted, and a missing intermediate directory still fail closed.

### W385 nonempty snapshot recovery anchor task card (2026-11-10, in progress)

Entry: with the async grant fix, `W385_NONEMPTY_SNAPSHOT_PROBE=1` now fails at the ordinary `write-nonempty-snapshot-cli` source-lock reclamation assertion. `checkpointRecoveryAnchor` skips only `session_color`, `title`, `file_history`, verified text turns and inert display pairs; a nonempty snapshot inserts `directory_snapshot_intent`, per-entry `directory_snapshot_observation` rows and `directory_snapshot` between the user and assistant turns, so the anchor stops at the turn end. `completedCheckpointSnapshotAnchor` additionally requires `paths.length === 0` and `entries.length === 0`. `reconcileResumedCheckpointInheritance` therefore finds no torn/branch head and does not reclaim.

Source: rehosted file-history bodies `rhe` [4728518,4730433), `Tke` [4732048,4733481) and `Ole` [4694145,4697475) in manifest-verified `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js` (SHA-256 `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`, zero-based half-open UTF-16). They build the in-memory `trackedFileBackups` snapshot state and load transcript rows; they define no host source-lock reclamation or durable backup proof. This remains an S3 host adaptation.

Design constraint: the pure event anchor cannot verify backup bytes. A session-level verified walker must check, for each snapshot turn, owner/messageId/timestamp agreement, `intent.paths` equals `snapshot.entries` paths, matching observation rows, no `interrupted`/`preCheckpoint`, a complete text turn, and every present/missing reference through the session's backup store; `unknown`/unreadable entries refuse. The same walker must serve the reclamation head and `checkpointRecoveryPrefix`, or the torn-prefix comparison will disagree. Do not widen `checkpointRecoveryAnchor` alone.

Prototype and finding: a session-level `verifiedSnapshotSuffix` walker was implemented (structure/observation/backup checks) and reverted before delivery. Instrumentation on the opt-in probe showed the suffix after the torn recovery is a **blocked external Write tool turn first** (`user`, assistant `tool_use`, `tool_effect` error, `tool_result`, observers, assistant text, `turn_end`), then the snapshot turn. The pure anchor stops at the tool turn, so snapshot verification alone cannot reclaim; the nonempty snapshot case is coupled to the still-open **tool-effect/no-effect provenance** requirement. The walker is not sufficient and was removed; product identity remains `3fea20e689ae64680a788c305d87807b6e57ea68931e0890e0f9647736364691`.

Blocked-turn evidence (2026-11-10): the CLI's blocked external Write turn journals `tool_start` (writeInputDigest and runtimeWriteOwner), six `runtime_wrapper_observer` rows, `runtime_write_execution` entered/completed, a `directory_backup` for the already existing target, `tool_effect` with the file-exists error, `tool_result`, and two `tool_result_observer` rows. The backup is a capture, not a write; there are no `directory_publication_*` rows and the target bytes are unchanged. Caller-controlled observers/callbacks can still create effects after the result row while leaving the same observer shape, so this journal does not distinguish a benign host observer from an effectful caller. The conservative source-lock retention is therefore correct; the positive probe expectation is blocked on observer/callback/hook effect provenance (a capability or attestation), not on snapshot verification.

Next: design that provenance/capability before reconsidering the probe; retain the nonempty snapshot and the blocked tool turn meanwhile. Do not widen the pure anchor, the snapshot walker or no-effect classification without it.

### W385 nonempty snapshot positive-probe diagnosis (2026-11-09, open)

Opt-in `W385_NONEMPTY_SNAPSHOT_PROBE=1` on `CLI restart preserves recovery uncertainty across writer death` fails first in scenario `write-nonempty-snapshot-cli-async` at the hidden-effect assertion, not at the source-lock assertion. The diagnostic suffix shows the async `PostToolUseFailure` lifecycle started, a `tool_effect`, a `tool_result` and both `tool_result_observer` rows committed, but the detached hook's `hiddenEffect` file is absent after the resumed CLI has exited 0. A temporary five-second poll in the fixture did not observe the file either, so this is not a simple late-write race. A temporary instrumentation then showed the resumed session still carries the `PostToolUseFailure` async hook configuration and the CLI made two provider calls, but the hook script's first-statement start marker never appeared. The async command was therefore not launched (or failed before its first statement); the missing effect is at hook wiring, not at late delivery. The CLI provider fixture waits for that file before its second turn, so the absence means the detached effect is cancelled, not configured on the resumed path, or otherwise not produced; it is not evidence about ordinary nonempty-snapshot reclamation. The non-probe lock-retention expectation remains the accepted regression. Wiring path: `runHooks` skips `async: true` commands unless `options.startAsyncCommand` is supplied (`hooks.ts` around 1766). The standalone Agent used for the test's source session does not supply it; the interactive and headless CLI Agents pass `runtime.hookOptions` (`interactive.ts` around 1358, `cli.ts` around 1006), and the runtime binds `AsyncHookRegistry.start` (`runtime.ts` around 1826). A temporary marker confirmed the resumed CLI reaches `startAsyncCommand` for `PostToolUseFailure` with no thrown error, but the shared `/bin/sh -c` spawn in `startHookCommand` was never observed. The isolated probe `.audit/w385-async-hook-start-probe.mjs` then ran the real `runHooks` plus `AsyncHookRegistry.start` with `journalOwner` omitted: the command spawned, wrote its marker, returned a background task id and completed with no additional context. The registry/command path therefore works in isolation; the CLI failure is in runtime wiring or owner context (journalOwner/session_id/workspace or the per-Agent hookOptions), not in the async command runner. Next capture owner, journalOwner, payload session_id and workspace at the resumed CLI boundary and compare them with the isolated case; if the standalone path remains unsupported, move the probe to a supported effect instead of weakening the reclamation rule. Never treat a missing effect as no-effect proof. Temporary runtime/hooks instrumentation was reverted and the build/identity restored to `dae257984bab4d296962e2a3296a4c0bb5833779143c2ae80cc58889755320f4`; no product change in this diagnosis.

### W385 #35 generic tool implementation pin (2026-11-09, verified bounded unit)

Entry: the factory preflight below left generic dispatch dependent on unproved reference stability. `.audit/w385-generic-tool-identity-probe.mjs` reproduced the gap: a real Agent replaced a custom tool's `execute` in the `status` callback after authorization and the replacement ran (`{"marker":true,"mode":"replaced","result":["REPLACED_RESULT"]}`). Source: manifest-verified `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js`, SHA-256 `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`, zero-based half-open UTF-16; Write `create(e)` starts at 736099 and binds `checkPermissions` [736116,736494), `validateInput` and `call` (738913) to one host; `GWo` (2272799)/`KWo` (2275902) dispatch that same instance. The host adaptation pins the selected implementation across the awaited permission/hook path.

Implementation: `snapshotToolImplementation` captures the prototype, the `execute` data descriptor and the optional `executeBlocks` data descriptor at five owned boundaries: Agent dispatch after `this.tools.get`, `bindRuntimeTool` construction, `bindScopedChildTool` construction, the model-hook tool-loop callback, and the MCP-hook callback. `executeAgentToolBody` checks the Agent snapshot in its generic branch; `bindRuntimeTool.execute`/`executeBlocks` check the construction snapshot after the refresh/check callbacks; `bindScopedChildTool` checks after its approval returns and before the generic handler; the two hook callbacks check immediately before `execute`/`executeBlocks`, covering a replacement during the `hook_tool` admission append. Builtin Write/Edit branches keep their existing specific checks and error text. CURRENT asked to compare the remaining tool factory and implementation identity obligations with the existing effective-input authorization before changing dispatch. This section records that comparison only; no dispatch, schema or recovery behavior changed.

The source therefore binds check and effect to one host `e` at creation and does not re-resolve an implementation by tool name at dispatch.

Host coverage today: `snapshotBuiltinMutationInput` (tools.ts 896-912) freezes the parsed scalar input and records the selected edit/raw-write handler; `rawWriteHandler` (882-891), `executeAgentToolBody` (1218-1224), `bindRuntimeTool` (1161-1180), `snapshotTool`/`matchesToolSnapshot` (1238-1266) and `isBuiltinReadFile` (1289-1306) pin the builtin Write/Edit handlers and `read_file` identity. Remaining obligations, found by static reading and not reproduced:
1. `executeAgentToolBody` line 1225 executes the generic `tool.executeBlocks ?? tool.execute` after authorization without a handler/method snapshot; only builtin Write/Edit take the pinned branches.
2. `bindRuntimeTool` line 1181 forwards generic `tool.execute` without a snapshot; the runtime wrapper is snapshotted only for Write.

Durable creation integration result, 2026-11-07, verified path; feature Partial. Normal mixed forward and inverse missing-file creators now use the shared two-phase coordinator. Skill output persistence investigation (2026-11-04, open). Rehashed against manifest: `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js` `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`, `iye` [3368429,3370821), Shell mapper [4335357,4336747), call/return [4340000,4347400); `chunk-566cpr3w.js` `bcbbf0cd8b6c5132409afe2e38ac723d8dd65dc466aadb50e9f10ea2b1dc06e4`, Vne through text-size functions [2128,7810); `chunk-phm7wwmz.js` `40e46cb899d8e325ee27e23dca0b298833a9b246ca314a282f860e768e6baf12`, constants [1312,1450); `chunk-dxp0113e.js` `489607d344859854d4cfae144a2e0bbd919fe3942778436ec0f0e14a3e10c5d9`, gqe/hJ [1416,1800). Coordinates are zero-based half-open UTF-16; ranges include surrounding declarations where indicated. Source `iye` calls Shell then GVe and substitutes mapped `content` when it is a string; arrays instead use Ypn on raw stdout/stderr. Shell's mapper prioritizes nonempty structured arrays and otherwise maps `persistedOutputPath` to a textual preview; Shell call may copy an output file to the session result directory before returning, while classified failures throw before that copy. Generic persistence measures text UTF-16 length, excludes image/document arrays, applies the tool-specific threshold and ceiling, persists text or text-only arrays and formats a 2000-character preview. Shell default `gqe()` is 30000 characters; configuration is clamped to 4000..128000 and feature override in Vne can change the threshold. Generic fallback threshold is 400000 and default persistence cap 1 GiB; storage-specific limits may further constrain it. Failed generic persistence normally returns the original result, while the special F_ storage branch may instead truncate textual content. These are static source observations, not proof of execution.

Host `expandedBody` owns per-command journal effects and replaces spans with `shellOutput` strings; the Darwin supervisor streams combined bytes and aborts above `maxOutputBytes`, while expanded body has a separate same-config byte cap. Runtime constructs the journal per workspace and owner; `Session.readFileState` is a read-file cache, not evidence of a tool-result output cache. Output file construction, cleanup, session storage path/identity and their source dependencies are not yet closed; no source-backed production port was selected or implemented. W385 keepalive production and Shell settlement (2026-11-01). Static source only. `E0` adds a reason to a copied set for an existing local agent; `II` removes it, schedules eviction for a terminal unretained agent when empty, and invokes the empty-set cleanup check. Ordinary asynchronous child launch and foreground-to-background handoff add `agent:<child>` to the resolved owner when the `ve()` gate permits; forked-skill launch adds the same form. Agent notification routes to a running or eligible parked owner and retains the reason while delivery is pending; otherwise it removes the reason and routes to the main owner. Completion can add `flag:idle-window` under its feature/background gates; failure and kill clear the set. These conditions are source observations, not a runtime ordering verdict.

Shell `Czr` passes the agent ID into launch and registration. Explicit background calls registration; timeout or turn-abort conversion uses `Xn`, which either converts an existing foreground task through `jRn` or registers a new one. `jRn` calls `WPn`, which adds `bash:<task>` and returns the settlement release callback. `GPn` flushes output, updates terminal state, claims the notification and queues it for non-monitor tasks before invoking release. Release preserves the reason only under its feature, owner-state and pending-delivery checks; otherwise it removes it. `ZWr` removes a pending matching notification when delivered as a tool result and removes the reason, with a returned rollback that restores both. Notification claim and actual queue delivery/interleaving are distinct. Host `selectChildTools` excludes background controls, `BackgroundRegistry.start` starts a new process without a child owner, and its own completion queue lacks the source delivery binding. Source owner identity, foreground process adoption and delivery/rollback remain unbound; no independent production slice or test was established.

Hook-boundary investigation (2026-11-06, open). The host may raise ordinary and classic `PermissionRequest` or `PermissionDenied` during authorization, `PreToolUse` before dispatch, `PostToolUseFailure` after an executed failure, and `PostToolBatch` after the paired results. An uninterrupted interval without `hook_start` excludes only ordinary starts journaled in that interval; it does not exclude classic handlers or an asynchronous hook launched earlier. `AsyncHookRegistry` has owner-scoped list/get/wait APIs, but the primary Runtime does not expose them as durable call evidence; a listed terminal state and a bounded wait do not by themselves prove that every completion callback has finished. Live config and loaded classic modules can change, and current journal rows do not bind their complete historical state or async job IDs. The real post-result async fixture above remains the execution evidence; this investigation changes no product behavior and does not establish a no-hook proof.

Different-session compiled PTY probe (2026-11-05, partial). `node scripts/smoke-agent-transcript-cli.mjs --directory-switch` uses owned loopback SSE and actual compiled CLI: create distinct existing B and A by `/clear`, `/add-dir` in A, model calls native descriptor `read_file`, and loader waits after the helper's opened-file metadata arrives. Real Ctrl-C kills the helper and unblocks the loader wait; after cancellation A switches by `/resume B`, B sends an actual new turn, then the loader release signal is sent. B request, screen and raw journal exclude the A secret; B request/journal also exclude A prompt and call ID. A audit prefix remains byte-identical and contains no secret, reflecting cancellation before effect write. Two separate compiled cold Session processes for each ID exclude the secret; helper PID exits, the original directory inode is no longer held by its original FD slot, and session locks/skill-effect leases are absent. This checks canceled helper isolation, not an old invocation returning after B: the loader wait is released by child.kill during cancellation. `--directory-switch --directory-switch-hold-through-cancel` deliberately suppresses that unblock; after Ctrl-C it times out at `cancel foreground Read`, showing `running tool: read_file`. Async-hook ownership and cleanup follow-up (2026-11-01). Static inspection; manifest entries 19 and 415 match module SHA-256 `chunk-4bw62nzm.js` `1a8788672a623975dc4a807604528e46b128f16b5ec159495c0ec2370f805713` and `chunk-sfn1dbxq.js` `4c74137eb23221981404d0ca87b765912f83344851d5c132b21857e5685b03da`. Coordinates are zero-based half-open UTF-16. `q` [10003,10147) indexes a WeakMap by object identity. `Bxr` [53194,53310) accepts a supplied host for a root; `ln` [53565,56759) uses the root's same host for a `withProject` fork. `fn` [76057,76383) constructs a new host and `Wi` [76383,76488) supplies it to a root; `B` [76502,76526) selects the contextual or default session. Thus a Wi-created root gets a new host and its project forks share it, while Bxr permits multiple roots to share a supplied host. This does not establish which constructors are used by every live entrypoint or map all host identities to product session IDs.

`_bt` [625103,625564) registers by `processId` with Map.set, replacing an existing key; `n4` [625591,625629) selects by current host; `kbt` [625629,626248) registers synchronously after progress setup. `CXo` [630243,630565) captures `values()` once, runs the captured handlers with Promise.all, and only then invokes `removeAll`, which clears both the entire current map and undelivered responses. A registration after the snapshot can therefore be cleared without being in the drain; replacement under a captured key does not replace the captured object. On a captured handler rejection, Promise.all rejects without cancelling the other handlers and the final clear is skipped. `WLe` [626254,626520) has no local catch: an exception from stopping progress, reading output, cleanup or publishing rejects its handler and prevents later steps in that handler. These are control-flow consequences, not observations of which underlying operations actually fail or the real scheduling frequency. The `bbt` excerpt [626520,629020) separately takes a snapshot and uses Promise.allSettled; its overlap with `CXo` has no established serialization here.

Host entrypoints pass `session.id` to `hookOptions` (`src/interactive.ts:1274`, `src/cli.ts:986`); `runtime.ts:1473-1495` keys its registry by that owner. `src/subagents.ts:137-180` instead owns a separate child registry and overrides the supplied async start callback, waits up to 200 ms, then closes it. Root/fork host-sharing and child registry isolation therefore have different documented shapes, but actual source context assignment, independent-root sharing, notification delivery and cleanup overlap remain open. No production slice is justified, and no product edit, runtime execution, network call or lane-binding review was performed.

This establishes these headless paths only, not all process exits or ordering relative to the separate `lts.shutdown` SessionEnd path.

In the latter module, `_bt` and `n4` [625103,625629) (`0eb4e24abd611dc0a5b5f0f19b14ca974cd22745302905631b72630d3fe5c919`) retain pending hooks and undelivered responses in a `q` keyed by `B().host`. `CXo` [630243,630565) (`05afcda0644737e057c93356f929bf7390ba1cd51297a36bb681a5f8a21cd966`) snapshots values and concurrently handles them: completed commands await their result and publish success/error; others are killed unless already killed and publish cancelled. `WLe` [626254,626520) (`7f900b22f8bcb2e8df9b8b331ab5c90e979d387880d7e88e0bf9a67feb27e568`) stops progress, reads output, cleans the shell handle and publishes. `removeAll` follows successful `Promise.all`, clearing both registry and held responses; rejection leaves that final clear unexecuted. Exact behavior of the delegated kill/output/publish on concurrent settlement remains unproven.

In ordinary `lts.shutdown` [101650,103256), slice `ed806c784aec1fe348acc970ce470288d311c21e2ce2e9bd4b33e63764ab86be`, the snapshot cleanup drain starts first and is awaited only until its 2000 ms race settles; `Tst` follows, then `Lvn` and `Wbt`; session-end hooks are followed by another `Lvn` and `Wbt`. ## Integration design

Keep the recovered analyser's state at module lifetime, as in the source: `E6` synchronously saves and restores its prefix state, while `A`, `j` and `P` remain monotonic counters. This replaces the per-check factory proposed by the scratch prototype and avoids resetting those counters. The local environment adapters set `wd` to false and `$Ts` to its no-reader default true. Retain the source's call-time `os.homedir()` for `ht`; when HOME is absent, this can differ from `/bin/sh`, and the caller must keep any existing incomplete-reading restriction rather than treat the inferred home as proof of the shell's value. A generated source-copy plan records all 146 original ranges and hashes, and the existing parser exports its already-copied `yyr` helper. The planned source result adapter must distinguish parser failure, a `too-complex` result, and a simple command array. It must carry the prefix-retention vector and each `pyr` sample separately. The shared `shellReadings.exhaustive` contract remains with the existing ordinary tree/text reader and the absent-HOME legacy guard; the new sampling completeness belongs only to permission combination. The existing host deny/ask/allow readers, hook-input recheck and approval owners remain in place. A sampled source result must preserve the original whole-line decision when checking the source command texts. An independent reader confirmed that each vector runs the entire `O3e`/`D3e` pipeline, with source early returns, path checks, subcommand checks and an object-sensitive `ior` merge. Treating each `commands[].text` as an ordinary top-level host decision would therefore be an unverified policy rewrite. Product integration remains gated on mapping those branches; the pre-change compiled baselines are recorded below. An owned factory prototype generated from the same 146 hash-bound ranges isolates state per instance; interleaved calls with two HOME values retain the expected old/new readings and return each owner's HOME. The product-shaped plan SHA-256 is `ecdcae6d6615f02712da2ba21586902f82625b4660f8486d0cb0318d0003d938`, generated candidate `7abf968890a43de84edd5f23e80d33bcb09ba761cc44f64c6013abc9ff27142f`, ledger `5e4c1d05a8bb26724fd56978f25b3e1884915a64ef2f4e873c7a36fff1a32563`, and runner `e87db9c35147388033dabe1047068afa88d0f32a69cebad4d1ed3b1c4a43cef1`. All 146 body hashes and text ranges match; the scope scanner reports zero unresolved names after TypeScript transpilation. Running the JavaScript-only scanner directly on a typed parameter failed before analysis; the transpiled candidate is the checked artifact. The prototype uses an exact copied `yyr` helper and the compiled parser. The ordinary per-vector policy remains unconnected.

## Vector policy review

An independent reader verified the source ordering through the `D3e` prechecks, semantics, sandbox, compound-command and multi-directory branches. Those branches precede the final per-command `jcn` check, so projecting every analyser `commands[].text` to a host `decideOnce` is not a source-equivalent implementation. For a conditional example, `cd /tmp; cd /var; rm target` reaches the multiple-directory branch before `jcn`, provided the path and nested-shell checks return no earlier result. Main verified that the copied `E6` returns three simple commands for that input and that `X=1 export Y; cd /tmp; cd /var; rm target` yields the same four commands in both prefix vectors. The host source execution returns deny for both commands in default and bypass modes when `Bash(rm target)` is denied. `Dcn` [3223957,3225417) and `bG` [3105028,3108425) were also inspected; the source rule-store, path and feature premises still need a controlled proof before asserting the source's final verdict. Source `VW`, `chunk-a60ee1ne.js` [4691,5003), body SHA-256 `3d607c8b197353a1d5c1eb7d919aa664c78998d42ff3e111fe77a0c9e958b80f`, returns a bypass-immune `outsideReadsBlocked` safety ask, which the current host `PermissionDecision` shape does not represent. `Agent.authorize` routes an ask without a `floor` into auto classification (`src/agent.ts:587`); a projection that drops the source's `classifierApprovable:false` and safety reason would therefore change that decision path. The final source mode wrapper and Hook recheck also consume the reason, so a safe adapter must preserve those distinctions end to end. Pipeline-to-command mapping and other early-return predicates remain open. A further source detail qualifies the conditional multi-directory example: `O3e` applies `$cn` [3253132,3253708), SHA-256 `724ee7599692796f6c6d2c7aa85f60073db9bb760955e046a46c5ff1be9f1743`, to its ask, and `$cn` rechecks the original line, `Kg` splits, subcommand-result keys and `ost` forms against deny/ask rules. A scratch copy of `Kg` [1072,1477) and its `m`/`E`/`D0` declarators [967,1007)/[1008,1051)/[1052,1058), `chunk-m00pavz3.js` module SHA-256 `e4dcdda42fdf15ff719179977326a414b62ad13d5992832859839c9203c16a62`, splits both candidate lines into their literal subcommands, including `rm target`. With a matching source deny rule and the stated earlier conditions, `$cn` therefore upgrades the multi-directory ask to deny. The independent reader's suggested final ask is refuted for this exact rule; the earlier `D3e` ordering is established but is not by itself a final-verdict counterexample. Copy-plan SHA-256 `954f9c3675893c164c318810b409e4cd875ec6a807210cda94b18b98e7bd1be2`, copied `Kg` fixture SHA-256 `fed031347b4199a2eb7fb85df93fd412f50dcca1f479f953618d8b449968db1d`; it reuses the compiled product parser. A generic deny-first loop still lacks source evidence for all of these branches. The recovered `ior`/`O3e`/`D3e` and their nested checks are asynchronous. Its `OAn` [3104531,3104568), SHA-256 `7de05c7da6d83c61b33f9b26330e93146ead854666d4fc5e3238a747c056a529`, uses an `AsyncLocalStorage` instance to suppress duplicate telemetry during sampled checks; the only other store read in this module is `dO` [3104568,3104621), SHA-256 `134cdfde186177d2a96a3fccba23a7f4bc68bd4ea54292bd22ae7debf6665515`. The no-telemetry host adaptation can omit that sink, but must retain sequential awaited vector evaluation and source result identity. The current `permissionDecision` is synchronous and is also used by synchronous diff-panel readers, so the future adapter needs a distinct async shell authorization boundary or an explicitly justified migration; replacing the shared signature alone would alter unrelated readers. Agent authorization, PermissionRequest updated-input rechecks, PreToolUse reauthorization, skills and child-registry wrappers are already asynchronous callers, while the child clamp is a separate precheck. Source `de`, `chunk-p46ep603.js` [4120,5234), SHA-256 `b36b198420ff43a4f53ccbb2a55e75946883b414595bba38684a341c59b52b88`, derives effective context at call time and overlays allowed/disallowed tools, command clamps, prompt settings, sandbox suspension, mode and working directory. The host's live owner and `effectivePermissionPolicy` must supply equivalent current state across every awaited vector, rather than a cached policy assembled before sampling. The migration inventory also includes the auto-mode post-classification recheck and its pre-hook floor check (`src/agent.ts:602` and `:897`), and the skill executor's independent `approve` wrapper (`src/skill-runtime.ts:74` and `:276`). Interactive skill invocation supplies a once-only confirmation callback (`src/interactive.ts:3867-3875`); headless CLI invocation supplies none (`src/cli.ts:1030-1031`), so both paths must retain their distinct approval behavior. Model-hook and MCP-hook tool checks use the same function but their catalogs are limited to named read-only file tools and read-only namespaced MCP tools respectively (`src/agent.ts:292-346`), and their execution contexts disallow shell; they do not consume the local shell decision path. Source `$pn` and `yk` first parse via `Zwe` [3355651,3356264), SHA-256 `95e29a86fccb34d21a6068f2a631fba82b957a75beca62b96f3bfe365873fc1a`, including a feature-gated unrecognized-key path; the host currently parses `runCommandSchema` at execution (`src/tools.ts:1190`) after `permissionDecision`. Any async migration must specify malformed inputs and cancellation at the permission boundary rather than silently adopting either ordering. These are identified consumers, not a completed migration.

## Narrow integration review

A separate static reader traced the literal-prefix policy path through `ior`, `O3e`, `D3e` and `jcn`, conditional on successful parsing, exact rule matching, no clamp or read block, and nonblocking semantics/path/nested-shell checks. It confirmed the three-prefix all-allow result at the `ior` layer and the four-prefix soft-ask downgrade to passthrough at that same layer. It did not independently close `$pn` or the full helper graph, and its premise excluding semicolons does not cover the recorded three/four-command examples. An owned compiled analyser probe confirms single-command controls `A=1 B=2 C=3 export X` and `A=1 B=2 C=3 D=4 export X` have three/eight/exhaustive and four/six/incomplete readings respectively; the compiled host returns allow for each with an exact content allow. Every sampled vector remains simple and retains the literal command text. An owned compiled adapter that deliberately returns allow for each vector yields `ior` allow after nine calls for three prefixes and passthrough after seven calls for four. These inputs fit the reader's no-semicolon premise, but the adapter is a fixture, so its path, rule and final-entry assumptions still apply. The reader rejected a hand-written special case that produces those decisions without porting the source policy body. The separately recorded `$pn` trace supplies a conditional final ask for ordinary mode and no whole-tool allow; complete policy equivalence remains open.

## Independent source-port review

A read-only reviewer regenerated both plans from the extracted modules, verified all 146 analyser and ten merge body ranges and ledgers, checked the parser export and generator, and confirmed the source `Rl` other-reason branch matches the local merge adapter. The review found no source-copy mismatch; it did not run tests, build or the CLI. It identified missing durable assertions for the exact four-prefix vector order and merge message, which main added to the existing three test groups; the focused 11 tests and TypeScript check pass after that test-only change. The review also identified unresolved HOME and feature-state equivalence, non-ASCII source/runtime coordinate equivalence, and policy/child/hook integration. The Unicode test is an observation of the copied source with the product parser, not proof of original runtime equivalence. The reviewer made nine tool calls against the requested eight; this does not expand its reviewed scope.

The compiled workflow-to-child baseline exposed a host data-shape defect before the child started. `workflow-script` normalized a flat `bashCommandClamp` list into one group, then `AgentRegistry.launch` rejected that nested list when it revalidated the external option. Source `chunk-hedqf2m1.js` SHA-256 `01fea1c4f8ed9442ca18c30704c8533a1f037b800cc4faae2b4ecaaa273f5a56` validates, deduplicates and sorts the flat list at UTF-16 [46284,47451), then adds it as a single permission layer at [62642,62783). The host workflow bridge now forwards that flat validated list and the child registry still performs its own validation and groups it. The targeted workflow option test and TypeScript check passed. After rebuilding, the owned compiled workflow reached the child command and reproduced the expected old-gate mismatch: `command echo clamped-ok; printf second` was denied as one unmatched line despite source `fTr` matching both segments. The compiled driver and the PermissionRequest rewrite regression provided pre-integration baselines; the source-copy review and integrated driver subsequently passed as recorded below. An owned compiled helper probe with `HOME` absent found `fTr` accepts `$HOME/bin/echo escaped` if its group contains both that literal text and `${os.homedir()}/bin/echo escaped`, while `/bin/sh` expands the absent variable to empty and would resolve `/bin/echo`. `E6` `Z` [68158,68694) assumes `os.homedir()` for HOME even when the shell environment has no HOME. With a whitespace-containing HOME, the unquoted expansion is instead unverifiable. This is a source/host execution discrepancy: a source-matched command can name a different executable. The integrated boundary preserves the legacy `shellReadings`/`clampAdmits` decision whenever HOME is absent, then applies copied `fTr`; for a present HOME, it pins that exact value in the individual tool call so a later environment change cannot invalidate the check. This is a host adaptation to preserve the existing restriction, not a claim that the source has that guard. Both the original and PermissionRequest-updated inputs get a check. The chosen value reaches only the executing tool context and is not written to the journal; unrelated environment fields retain their existing behavior. This probe executes no supplied shell command.

At the source outer boundary, `sor` [3208689,3208983) returns a deny if a shell permission check throws while any `bashCommandClamps` remain, and the shell definition calls it from `permissionCheckFailureDecision` [4337559,4337643). `EJo` [3208297,3208689) denies execution surfaces that cannot match the clamp. The host child pool currently removes `run_background` and `monitor` through `PARENT_CONTROLS`; its `authorize` function already checks a non-string command as unverifiable. Any child-gate migration must preserve those boundaries and keep an unexpected source-check exception from reaching execution. Source `O3e` performs `fTr` before `D3e`, with the same JSON-stringified failed span currently used by `bashCommandClampDenial`; it reads the current context's clamp groups on each call. The source workflow child adds a `{kind:"bash_command_clamp",rules:be}` permission layer after existing layers (`chunk-hedqf2m1.js` UTF-16 [62642,62783), declarator), and `de`, `chunk-p46ep603.js` [4120,5234), appends each such layer to `bashCommandClamps` in order. ## Sampled-denial integration plan

Environment binding follow-up: an owned skill invocation preflights `X=old; X=new export Y; printf "$HOME" > marker.txt` with `HOME=/allowed-fixture` and a deny for `printf /denied-fixture`. Approval of a later `true` changes HOME; the first command then writes `/denied-fixture` despite the deny. No recovered entrypoint was executed. Source `iye`, chunk-sfn1dbxq.js [3368429,3370821), SHA-256 `b7e7d086e93c72e32742a77033691e893b73479b7aa477dc794b6ff0759ecd56`, checks each span via `Bu` and then calls the shell tool; source `Z`, chunk-zjewzgfh.js [68158,68694), SHA-256 `a3e16a9b07f2129860dc33a00ecc4b95faf0096225c97876bd41dd0fb18f6ab9`, reads HOME from the host at analysis time. The host executes spans sequentially after preflighting all of them, an existing W06 adaptation. Bind the HOME value observed for each approval to that command's owned child environment so later callbacks and spans cannot change the value on which its sampled denial relied. Keep the source tool-call boundary and host preflight, allow a fresh value for each span, and preserve missing HOME as missing. Verify by rerunning the skill fixture, including an unaffected control and sequential approval values. An owned `Agent` probe then changed HOME from `/allowed-fixture` to `/denied-fixture` in the `tool: <name>` status callback after permission checking. `run_command`, `run_background` and command `monitor` each executed the latter value under a `Bash(printf /denied-fixture)` denial. Bind the HOME observed by each successful authorization to its execution context, replacing it if a hook changes the command and it is reauthorized. The existing foreground clamp already passes `shellHome`; extend that handoff to ordinary shell commands and consume the same value in the background registry. Preserve WebSocket monitor behavior and allow a later tool call to obtain a fresh value. Unknown-HOME probe: passing the source marker `__TRACKED_VAR__` as the analyser's `ht` value makes plain `"$HOME"` and `X=$HOME` vectors too complex, while the independent `$X` example still yields `printf old` and `printf new`. This is not a complete unknown-value representation: `"prefix$HOME-suffix"` yields the simple candidate `printf prefix__TRACKED_VAR__-suffix`, and an input deny `printf prefix*-suffix` matches that marker as if it were a value. An assignment to another declaration can likewise leave the marker in `envVars` and generated text while later `$X` candidates remain useful. A literal `__TRACKED_VAR__` also occurs in legitimate source text, so a blanket substring check would conflate it with a marker. The source `Z` [68158,68694) and `it` [61892,64542) distinguish tracked values through `Vs` [3597,3648), all in the verified `chunk-zjewzgfh.js` and UTF-16; the host's Boolean sampled-rule projection does not carry that distinction. These in-memory copied-analyser probes show why substituting a third magic HOME alone would neither close the runtime gap nor preserve deterministic denials. An additional probe places `printf "$HOME"` before the declaration: under the marker, `E6` stops before it records any declaration-prefix count, so simply catching the unknown sample also loses a later deterministic `printf new` denial. With HOME after the declaration, some deterministic candidates remain visible, but not every ordering. A proposed object-coercion sentinel also fails to model the plain quoted HOME read: `Z` returns the non-string object and `it` passes it through before any coercion, so no callback fires. For `FOO=$HOME env`, the copied assignment parser accepts that object as a partial assignment and creates `undefined=undefined env` instead of an unknown result. A non-string sentinel therefore violates the analyser's string contract. A direct host decision probe with a nonmatching HOME deny and bypass mode returns a readings ask for Bash indirect `${!H}` and `${HOME:-none}`, but allows a simple quoted `$HOME` when its chosen value does not match. These examples do not establish full coverage of indirect expansion or arbitrary shell syntax. The sentinel experiment therefore does not supply a viable attribution mechanism. This is static host mapping, not an integrated fix.

Inputs `9c2aef976384254937220500907d6f516270c12d9edee1976684b63a21a6b6ee`, validation `04937509b1673f63c223ad135e3bd64f44a375a55dd496d591b08aa7f2afe997`, build `7c2cf16ff63f611db9199f8c5b87f95ce9944e71331ff16d4684954fef13f2ce`. The local peer-file consumer adapts source `we`, `chunk-8t44px9f.js` SHA-256 `7d5f2f127553dea804c9345f9e1515b077ad7f4c42c5b5f81b1b6ce261bc48e3`, [22797,31590), body SHA-256 `256ad6e089aad893d86e440569930ab7577365ed6da88f813d9069f864b474cc`, UTF-16, whose `checkPermissions` applies `IA(et(path), permissions)` to each file. A later owned peer-file fixture used a distinct execution workspace with an ancestor link to a denied target. The original direct `send_peer_files` precheck used the rule workspace and returned instead of rejecting; both existing Read checks now receive the tool context workspace, and the three peer-file tests pass without a send attempt for that case. This source-backed S-6 adapter is included at `adb0e3ad`; independent candidate review remains pending. The existing `smoke-approval-retarget-cli.mjs --baseline` was rerun on the earlier `42c83fbf` build and again confirms all 18 stable, retarget and direct-denial observations across the six file tools. It confirms the separate approval-to-use defect remains; it is not a passing fix. The same driver without `--baseline` was subsequently run on `adb0e3ad` and failed at the first `read_file/retarget` case because the result contained `PROTECTED_FIXTURE` instead of an error. Later cases were not executed in that acceptance run; the separate baseline covers them. The non-baseline driver was rerun after the plan and hook recheck repairs at product/build identity `7e8be1b6`; it again failed at `read_file/retarget` with `PROTECTED_FIXTURE`, and later acceptance cases were not reached. A separate `--baseline` run on the same build records all 18 stable/retarget/direct outcomes across the six tools; all six retargets still reach their protected fixture. That baseline is a reproduced failure observation, not acceptance. A later bounded independent review returned `VERIFIED_SCOPED` for the four core decision files and `test/path-leaf-permission.test.ts`; its five per-file hashes match the candidate, and it reran the focused test 5/5 without a reproduced high-impact regression. It did not inspect peer integration, cross-platform behavior, complete policy ordering, CLI or the approval-to-use gap. It identified untested callers that omit the workspace argument and untested tilde/non-NFC paths; these remain follow-up questions, not confirmed defects. A main-only follow-up `a363b5360b58cd8c8873315ddaee4667016c37fc2f0b343f8cd33bd3b28ba3e3` explicitly changes a live session update's rule workspace to a parent while its diff project remains the child. The real `InlineDiffDialog` and `DiffPanel` denial callbacks then both miss a child alias whose protected landing an explicit child-workspace permission check denies. The ordinary `Session.open` seeds its owner with the child workspace. A later owned fixture `8f64b34ba19741da85804ca68fa1c8b84006e0597767bf47f02f9d36c0e1f3d1` reaches the same state through actual `relocateSession` with `sourcePlanTools:true`; `carryForkPermissions` retains the parent's `ruleWorkspace`, and both real callbacks return false while an explicit child-workspace permission check denies. This establishes the host relocation-to-callback path, not that a rendered diff contains the protected file. Source diff-consumer semantics and rendered reachability need mapping. Peer review, platform/root ownership, source-complete policy and approval-to-use binding remain open.

Open cleanup adapter boundary: an owned in-memory probe `f2e461c6f0eed5b6a448249483b3ff9d717e8fc539207d3cd14b808a6fa4ca75` wraps the copied `QHt`'s supplied `Pe` handle and catches every `close()` rejection, under `node --unhandled-rejections=strict`. The aborted, late-arriving handle no longer terminates the probe, but a normal successfully returned handle also suppresses its later close error. That blanket wrapper therefore changes the live-handle error contract and is not accepted as production adaptation. A second source-adapted scratch probe `f5a35c13a89d1bd78075ea3eb59d0e3e3b3a6db259c5a6cef90a483d7caa9eb3` adds a rejection handler only to the late-close promise. Under strict rejection handling it reports the orphan's close failure, preserves a returned handle's close failure and open failure, and skips opening when already aborted. The supplied reporting callback is synchronous and nonthrowing in this probe. This is a feasibility sketch only; the production owner, a throwing logger, nested `Z3` behavior and real cancellation have not been verified.

A bounded independent reader inspected the leaf-link candidate at `f6d0a613` and found no reproduced defect in its stated terminal-link scope. The reader ran the three focused groups and 12 compiled CLI cases, checked the `sNe` plan and call order, and identified an early-denial semantic change plus uncovered ancestor-loop and future missing-workspace boundaries. It did not regenerate the plan, verify the original artifact digest, run check/build, or run the 84/169 suites and approval-retarget driver. A follow-up owned Agent fixture `ba3c929936b5329a20ae9b0bfae23e83fcefcd33add736bcfdbcd9accb88f179` confirms the early-denial effect for a U+FFFD path: the local write is denied before its configured PermissionRequest hook can rewrite the input to `safe.txt`; neither hook marker nor safe file is created. The copied source `di` returns a resolved observation for the owned missing U+FFFD name, and source `ek` in verified `chunk-wh2vcbh8.js` SHA-256 `4f11ef8e1e1749cb96813db9575a40fad7d44576d313172aaa372c4baf330b68` [4200,4269), body SHA-256 `1e8c5321688ec55960f00972cb8cca3b4bac45bd3e283739f4f56899504787a6`, calls `et` and checks round-trip equality. An independent static follow-up traced `c_`, `Al`, `xBo` and `n2e`. `c_` denies an unresolved landing via `Al`; `xBo`, `chunk-fyhzvvp0.js` SHA-256 `1392b254e378432c7206e82a258512a740c26ce57263941ba3be4eb279675d19`, [8410,14040), body SHA-256 `9eb3fe5a4110c74df42f7e8b8de9eaa42c3229a0769e6ccf21d56d79691abef1`, returns an existing allow or deny before the PermissionRequest path. Its `n2e` [15475,16947), body SHA-256 `547937869c3d431cf7360a71ca09ef93456219a3cb5d5981a96f77a43a068ef6`, rechecks an updated input. These ranges are zero-based half-open UTF-16. The reader statically derived resolved/ask for a missing U+FFFD path and deny for an ancestor loop, with an unreadable ancestor depending on whether a link was followed; it did not run the complete source gate or hook, or exhaust its rule and safety predicates. A separate host probe shows that both `leafWriteDecision` and `contentRuleMatches` invoke `resolveChain` and reject the U+FFFD input. `contentRuleMatches` already did so at HEAD before the leaf adapter; without a policy the new leaf adapter introduces the same early rejection. Thus the tested configured-policy hook failure is a host/source candidate that predates the leaf adapter, not evidence that the adapter alone caused that exact fixture. Both paths need source-backed reconciliation while retaining the existing execution-time `nonCanonicalText` contract. The bounded correction uses source `di` for the leaf adapter, with its filesystem owner injected from the host workspace, and supplies the same observation to file-content matching within a single permission decision. Rule roots continue to come from their original layers. All host rule buckets also retain the host walk's additional intermediate spellings. This preserves both a pre-existing two-link denial and an allow rule's requirement to cover the intermediate name; source-only matching changed both in new failing regressions. The additional walk is a separate compatibility observation and is not an approval-time snapshot. An unresolved write observation follows copied `Al` ordering before `sNe`; calls without an applicable content rule still observe the path for the write leaf check. The host file tools retain `resolveChain` and its execution-time restrictions. The platform facade, empty-ask-hook rewrite, direct invalid execution, explicit target deny, link loop and isolated-child rule root need focused tests and an actual compiled CLI check before acceptance.

A separate owned macOS interleaving fixture `d44f20e87bad80ef1d306cb47a5b49869b1d4248dd03e34c17f6abd3634409a8` composes the copied `US` pin with the actual compiled `atomicWriteFile`. A separate owned interleaving runs the actual compiled `notebook_read` tool with an ordinary approved path. An owned deterministic interleaving against the actual compiled `atomicWriteFile` moves the public directory after the staged file is closed and substitutes a link to a protected directory before the writer's identity check. It establishes that the current kept-content error can report an inaccessible old pathname after movement; a publication adapter must retain or report recovery evidence according to its own verified contract.

A separate descriptor-relative publication experiment on macOS arm64 used an owned C fixture, SHA-256 `f4f4714f3623dc9771313886c5a5dfb265f609f9be385401851e43d3bca81c9f`, compiled with `clang -std=c11 -D_DARWIN_C_SOURCE -Wall -Wextra -Werror`. It opened an approved directory with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, staged and measured the content with `openat`/`fstat`, replaced the directory pathname with a link to another owned directory, then called `renameat` using the held directory descriptor for both names. The moved approved directory received `NEW` and the replacement directory retained `PROTECTED`. The fixture cleaned its files. An extended version, SHA-256 `48d4e6d8ffc0a957fe20860abd98b65c534e3a6634a2180e5d2a04c645fff289`, also forces `renameat` to fail with `ENOENT` and then verifies that the staged `KEPT` bytes remain accessible through `openat` on the held descriptor before cleanup. A separate macOS C fixture `a1634c8d8ca34d4a2690db74a40834f43f355aa2601368e61c99c23fe9e56ee6` observes that `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` on a held directory returns its new pathname after rename; after removal it still returns a pathname but `stat` of that pathname fails. This succeeds while the new pathname stays stable. Recovery-path reporting still needs to verify the returned path's identity and handle concurrent movement or removal; these fixtures do not establish an always-available retained-content path. These are deterministic syscall-level observations; they do not exercise product authorization, package installation, error-message preservation, the source writer or other platforms. An additional Node probe found `/dev/fd/<directory-fd>/file` returned `ENOENT` on this host, so that spelling is not a substitute for `openat`/`renameat` here. Node `v26.10.0` did not expose `fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW_ANY` or `O_CLOEXEC`; the installed macOS SDK defines them as `0x20000000` and `0x01000000`, respectively, matching the values observed in source `chunk-8pet3bvp.js` SHA-256 `aff6bcfc21f2613576b751f7d19d89c0059fc4eb1ae6af3a60381555a783bcf4`. The source `wGn` capability probe [3034,3275), body SHA-256 `afce3d145ff56377c135d8e078bc65a1a2a006896ee013646062b78848f726fb`, is UTF-16 and remains a runtime capability check, not a universal platform guarantee. An additional Node fixture `28937506aba46faa89ce6abb68b44c036a35216baa55aafb041efb17db98b03e` opens an owned real directory with those numeric flags and gets `ELOOP` for its symlink spelling. It tests this host only and does not establish how to publish through the descriptor from Node. The current Node file API and macOS peer-identity addon expose no such publication operation; implementing one would add a native package/build dependency and needs an explicit source-adaptation contract and fail-closed fallback before product integration. The existing `scripts/build-native.mjs` builds `peer.node` only on Darwin and skips when headers are absent; `package.json` ships that compiled addon and its C source, while `smoke-package.mjs` installs with `--ignore-scripts`. A second native capability cannot assume install-time compilation or Linux coverage, and reusing the peer addon's optional load failure as permission to use a pathname writer would leave the publication boundary unbound. Any adapter must make capability absence and the portability contract explicit and validate the packed artifact.

A follow-up expiry fixture, SHA-256 `410f0f7fb0ddc95ef6fdd186a91a2ee3ce91f8a946922719f93dc1d41c2a40e0`, confirms that consuming an unrelated empty-path key does not clear a different evicted key: its first `mY` lookup raises the source expiry error and the second falls back to fresh resolution. A later in-memory probe, SHA-256 `91925a81e6f527c6909fb0a0bdb42b3516ee0f0d2d52ed3e3fa232828a07a9bb`, supplies separate invocation tokens and marks a wrapper retired before deleting its matching live and evicted keys in both lanes and its read identities. A separate saturation case confirms the copied lane's `poisoned` bit remains true after retirement and makes a missing fresh lookup return `j8e`; clearing individual entries must not clear that uncertainty. This probe directly manipulates copied `Be` fields and is not an integrated owner, does not solve global poison recovery, or prove all cancellation/concurrency paths. Source `Go` invokes `onReprompt` with that input and decision, and `Ie` replaces its displayed input and result before rebuilding the dialog. Main independently read those branches and the `i1t` callers in `chunk-24k7d6mw.js` and `chunk-kwdhpnes.js`; the coordinator `i1t` [4681,5320), body SHA-256 `9386f202ef5ffcf8e2eb650da1d7fe2a3ccfa785d13d9fe1df0017ad57f817da`, may instead discard a reprompt result and continue the original dialog, so its scheduling path must remain distinct. The `Go` reprompt dispatch excerpt [45300,45560) has SHA-256 `f2dc7864d27153735d7455c0ecb77eb6814142076ba2f8a28a4e383c61f3ac4c`, and the `Ie` callback excerpt [53050,53650) has `3eeb53036f5879b66bf76adeb06f95de7f68f8fb9ad88d9064b3127f74929642`; both are excerpt rather than complete-function digests. Source `kxr` contains `ExitPlanMode` and `AskUserQuestion`; on changed input with no `mcpInfo` those names bypass only `GAn`'s interaction ask, not a rule ask. The corresponding host `submit_plan` has no established `kxr` source identity. The reader verified module hashes, source ranges and name bindings without running the source application. The source `ExitPlanMode.requiresUserInteraction` also depends on its team/agent state, whereas the host flag is static. The host's current universal `floor:'rule'` denial matches the observed no-prompt `sxr` path but not the interactive dialog's reprompt path; the 12-case baseline below confirms the current CLI denies a rewritten rule ask even with an interactive callback. The local no-rewrite hook currently reaches a distinct tool interaction rather than the source coordinator's original permission dialog. Host `interactiveLoop` supplies a permission callback, but resident-worker mode also constructs that callback while `readAnswer` rejects terminal input. Headless CLI, registry children and foreground skill agents do not supply it; tool-level question/review callbacks are a separate surface. Callback presence therefore is not by itself a complete prompt-availability test. Source `vC`, `chunk-40cepjpq.js` module SHA-256 `473c9dfb84c9defcb7ca5bd5e6f598cd951274dc2c1334a67c8b9d25b451a8b2`, starts at UTF-16 offset 121081; its observed child-context branch at 124876 sets `awaitAutomatedChecksBeforeDialog` when `isAsync` is true and prompts remain available. `Go` runs hook results concurrently with the dialog only when that flag is false, while the earlier `i1t` coordinator returns null for a reprompt result before the original dialog is created. This is an additional source scheduling boundary, not proof that every host callback has the same mode. A bounded repair must preserve both owned host interaction and explicit rule approval while distinguishing actual prompt-capable and no-prompt owners; the exact dialog/coordinator mode, user edits, cancellation, updates and PermissionRequest re-entry require coverage. A narrow host design for the synchronous local callback is to carry the rewritten input and the new rule-ask reason into one explicit user approval, then continue with that input only after the callback allows; the no-prompt path keeps the current denial. The `PermissionRequest` hook is not rerun by the source `Ie` reprompt callback. For a prompt-capable main session the candidate host state would be one mutable request `{input, reason, signal}` with a boolean answer, while a no-prompt owner retains the current deny; the existing owner API does not expose whether an available callback represents a human dialog or a closed resident input. ## Invalid lane-binding review rerun (2026-11-01)

The original review stopped on an API cybersecurity-risk flag and produced no verdict. A later rerun changed the model or agent to bypass that interruption. The rerun is invalid as an independent review. The retained claims below, including all findings, absence claims, test counts, type-check and probe results, are unverified and must not be used as evidence. They are preserved solely as a record of the invalid rerun. Earlier independent records remain separate.

The rerun claimed the following findings:

1. **High, pre-existing and still open.** No production tool consumes `pathApprovalCall`. `TrustedReadContract`, `AsyncReadHandleConsumer`, `AsyncReadPermissionCheck`, `prototypePermissionDecision`, `recordObservedRead`, `takeVerifiedRead` and `readTrustedHandleLines` have test-only callers (`rg` over `src` returns only definition files and this owner module). `isBuiltinReadFile` returns false for the `bindRuntimeTool` wrapper the agent actually receives, so a contract can only be built inside the `readFileTool` closure; it cannot be built from the context's wrapped tool. The six-tool approval-to-use hole therefore remains open, and `test/agent-lifecycle.test.ts:1896` records the current bypass rather than fixing it.
2. **Medium, new.** `PathApprovalCall.take` (`src/path-approval-call-owner.ts:342`) and `finish` (`:364`) call `stash.consume(entry.key, path, 'read')` after the write-lane consume. `Be.consume` (`src/path-approval-stash-source.ts`) deletes by the `${key}\0` prefix, and each lane entry owns its own `${callKey}:${randomUUID()}` key, so the write entry's key never matches the read entry's key. The call is a no-op and "write consumption clears the read lane" is unimplemented. A probe confirmed it: after `record('read','/p')` and `record('write','/p')`, `take('write','/p')` returns saved and a later `take('read','/p')` still returns saved. No cross-call deletion occurs because keys are per-call UUIDs and are not prefixes of one another.
3. **Low/medium.** `recordObservedRead`/`takeVerifiedRead` (`:296-353`) trust caller-supplied identity and only re-`stat` the observed landing. Safety depends on `eMt` rejecting changed spellings at open time; the names overstate the guarantee. They are marked legacy and unconnected.
4. **Low/medium.** In `AsyncReadHandleConsumer`, a successful `check()` followed by no `readLines()` leaves the `AsyncReadPermissionCheck` lane and its abort listener until abort or `open()`. `permissions.ts:686` captures identity only on macOS while `openReadSnapshot` supports Linux, so on non-macOS `open()` will always fail with `Read approval identity expired`; the platform-specific tests are `skip: !MACOS`.
5. **Low.** The model-hook (`agent.ts:342`) and MCP-hook (`agent.ts:374`) paths classify pre-execution failure as `error`, while the main path reports `denied` (`:1049`). `ended` is diagnostic only and does not affect authorization.
6. **Low.** `identityReservations` is shared across active calls (cap `entriesCap * 2`, default 512) and the `Be` stash capacity is shared, so concurrent calls can evict each other and force `expired`. This direction is fail-closed; the agent currently executes tool calls sequentially.
7. **Low.** `inertSchema` does not clear `seen` when a nested value throws, and copies non-index own enumerable array properties that `JSON.stringify` ignores. `isBuiltinReadFile` additionally requires matching `execute` identity, `readOnly === true`, `Object.prototype` and a WeakMap registration, so neither has a security consequence.

The invalid rerun also claimed no counter imbalance, negative reservation, abort-listener leak, unhandled rejection, or cross-call stash deletion. It reported 441 related cases, a passing `tsc --noEmit`, and inline probes including 1000 record/take/finish cycles. All these claims and numbers are unverified. Item 49 remains open under the separate existing records.

W385 startup gate result (2026-11-03): `cc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 native/shell-supervisor/supervisor.c -o native/shell-supervisor/supervisor` exit 0; `node scripts/smoke-shell-supervisor.mjs` exit 0; `node --import tsx --test test/shell-supervisor-status.test.ts` exit 0, 3/3.
